q: Our furnace oil invoice is in litres. How do we convert it for emissions?
title: Furnace oil litres to kilograms
short: Multiply litres by the density on the invoice or test certificate to get kilograms, then apply the CO2 factor per tonne. IPCC defaults for residual fuel oil give about 3.13 tonnes of CO2 per tonne. Densities vary by grade and temperature, so use the supplier's figure rather than a guess.
audience: MSMEs using furnace oil or LSHS in boilers and furnaces

ol: Times density in kg per litre, from the invoice or certificate.
Times 3.13 t CO2 per tonne, or the supplier's carbon content if given.

p: IPCC default net calorific value of 40.4 GJ per tonne times 77.4 kg CO2 per GJ for residual fuel oil. It is a default; supplier test data is better.
Invoices quoting volume at a reference temperature, and tanker deliveries where the dip reading differs from the invoice.

senseible: Senseible reads fuel invoices, gas bills and delivery documents into dated, fingerprinted records, so each tonne of CO2 traces back to the document behind it.
